External Scan

Public HTTP/HTTPS websites through the same broad active engine: authenticated or unauthenticated crawling, input mutation, WAF detection and component intelligence.

Internal Scan

Localhost, LAN, private-IP and internal-DNS websites use the identical broad active profile as External Scan, including authentication, crawling, input probes, WAF checks and component intelligence.

Client-Side Edition: both modes use the browser fetch API directly from your device. Same-origin or CORS-permitting targets return full responses; anything the browser blocks is recorded per-request with its reason.
Client-Side transport ready — no server, no relay, no loopback ports. Evidence analysis works fully offline.

Conduit Native Server Route

Conduit Native owns all transport. When its bundled route is running, every request — crawler, active tests, Repeater, External and Internal scans alike — is fetched by the server: no CORS, no relays, your own IP. Internal targets (localhost/LAN) work through the route too, including on a custom port set in Conduit Native's Native Route panel (default 8787 — Kinetix auto-discovers the route on ANY port by probing all loopback ports, so no port needs to be configured). The route runs until you click Stop Native Route.

Server route status: not checked.
Port auto-discovery: initializing…
No manual port set yet — type the port you use and click “Use This Port” (it is verified live and used for every request).
There is no hardcoded port list in Kinetix. Requests go to, in order: the page's own origin (any port) → the ports you give here or via ?nativePorts=<port> → whichever port the background all-ports discovery (every port 1–65535 on 127.0.0.1 and localhost) confirms as the Native Route. So the route works on the exact port you set — and if it is (re)started later on a different port, Kinetix picks it up automatically (background rescan every 15 s while no route is known). Tuning: ?portScanFrom=/&portScanTo= (range), ?portScanHost=<ip1,ip2> (scan other hosts, e.g. a LAN IP), ?portScanInterval=<ms> (rescan period, 0 = off), ?portScanOff=1 (disable discovery). Watch the status bar: Native: ON improves transport reliability but is not required. If it is unavailable, Kinetix attempts direct browser transport and records only requests that the browser cannot read.
